page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Small damaged fragments in the lower left margin. The red band at the left edge and the dark band at the right edge are the scan edge and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: & in Phocicis, ubi iiii Bœotarchi decem millibus peditum gravis armaturæ, & equitibus quingentis præfuisse memorantur bello Græcorum contra Gallos: nec desunt alia apud autores alios. Nonnunquàm etiam uni tantùm summum imperium in bello commissum esse reperio, ut Pelopidæ, & eo capto Epaminondæ, item Cleomeni cuidam, de quo Pausanias,bello Thessalico contra Alexandrum Pheræum, ac rursum Epaminondæ in expeditione postremâ contra Lacones ac eorum socios, in quâ ipse periit. Vnicus apud Thucydidem locus est libro iiii, quem paulò antè citavi, qui ostendit, omnes Bœotarchos bello Attico Tanagræ cum Bœotis aliis, ex omnibus ejus regionis oppidis ibi congregatis, fuisse, ac de belli rebus consultasse: cumque cæteri Bœotarchi pugnam dissuaderent, Pagundam βοιωτάρχην ἐκ Θηβῶν [?], id est, Bœotarchum è civitate Thebanâ cum Ariontidâ Lysimachi filio, pugnandum suasisse & persuasisse. Hoc vero an ideò factum sit, quòd Tanagra Bœotiæ urbs, & quidem proxima esset, propemodùm in conspectu Thebarum, Aulidem & Delium versus, bi[?] Athenienses exercitus sui partem habebant, nescire me fateor. Id autem
Note: the left-margin fragments "nefiodi" and "neiue" are at the lower left and are not legible enough to transcribe.

page.notes: The line "uura" beginning "Tanagra", printed "Tana-" / "gra", has its "g" partly hidden; it is read as "gra". The Greek "βοιωτάρχην ἐκ Θηβῶν" is uncertain at the accents and is marked [?]. The word "bi" at the start of the line "bi Athenienses" is probably "ubi" with the initial letter damaged; marked [?]. The last line "fateor," is a catchword at the right foot. The left-margin fragments at the bottom are damaged and are not transcribed as text. I have not included them as notes because the letters cannot be read reliably. The red and dark bands at the edges are the scan edge and show-through, not printed text.
